documents.body:
OUTSIDE PSYCHIATRY GROUP
Medication check, 1/23/2024
Re: Paige Howland

Doing well through the holidays, spent two weeks at her parents' home. Mood stable. Therapy continuing weekly. No hallucinations or paranoid ideas reported. Nose concerns "in the background." No SI.

Sertraline 50 mg daily, adherent, no side effects. NKDA.

MSE unremarkable apart from mildly restricted affect.

Plan: no changes. Next visit in about 6 months.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28F for her physical. Steady year. Defending her thesis proposal this spring. Sees psychiatry twice a year and her therapist weekly, takes sertraline 50 every day. No voices. Sleeping 7-8 hours. Eats regular meals.

Exam: NAD, weight stable. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No thyroid enlargement. Skin fine. Mood euthymic per pt, affect slightly flat, logical.

PHQ-9 6.

Plan:
- Fasting lipids today, one-time screen at this age.
- Pap 2023 normal, next 2026.
- Flu and COVID in the fall.
- Continue psychiatry care as is.
See you in a year.

OUTSIDE PSYCHIATRY GROUP
Follow-up, 8/20/2024
Re: Paige Howland

Summer was quiet; working on data analysis for her dissertation. Mood fair, a few low days around deadlines. No perceptual disturbances. No suicidal thoughts. Therapy weekly. Body image worries ongoing, manageable.

Current medication: sertraline 50 mg daily. No adverse effects.

Plan: continue sertraline 50 mg daily, continue therapy, recheck in 6 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. Busy winter, dissertation writing. Feels more tired, mood "so-so." Still on sertraline 50 from psychiatry; last saw them in August, next visit not yet scheduled. Says therapy has been hit or miss lately because of her schedule. No voices. No thoughts of self-harm when asked.

Exam: well appearing, weight steady. HEENT, neck, heart, lungs, abdomen normal. Skin clear. Affect a little flat, thought process organized.

PHQ-9: 8 (up a bit from last year).

A/P:
- Mood: mildly worse with workload. Encouraged her to get the psychiatry follow-up on the calendar and protect her therapy hour. She will call them this week.
- Tdap today, last 2015.
- Pap next year.
RTC 1 year, sooner if mood slides.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Visit 5/28/2025, 16:45
Patient: Paige Howland, 29F

CC: brought by roommate for suicidal statements.

HPI: Roommate tells us that over the past month the patient has repeatedly talked about wanting to "end it all," has stopped going to her therapy appointments, and has been saving up her pills. Patient has schizoaffective disorder and body dysmorphic disorder and has been on sertraline for several years, previously stable. She tells me she has been isolating more and more this month and feels hopeless. She admits to collecting her medication. Denies taking any of it or any other act toward suicide today, but repeats that life is not worth living.

PMH: schizoaffective disorder, depressive type; body dysmorphic disorder; prior major depressive episodes. PSH: none.
Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother depression, maternal aunt bipolar, maternal uncle schizophrenia.
Social: graduate student, lives with roommate. Never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs.

Vitals stable throughout.
Exam: unkempt, avoids eye contact, speaks quietly in a flat monotone. Otherwise normal exam: heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft, no signs of ingestion or injury.

Labs: Na 140, K 4.1, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 98. TSH 2.5. Urine drug screen negative.

MDM: medically clear. Active suicidal ideation with means gathered. Emergency psychiatry consulted; she agreed to voluntary admission.

Disposition: admitted to inpatient psychiatry.
Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Inpatient Psychiatry Discharge Summary
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
INPATIENT PSYCHIATRIC UNIT, REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER
Admitted 5/28/2025, discharged 6/4/2025
Patient: Paige Howland
Legal status: voluntary

Admitting diagnosis: suicidal ideation in the setting of schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.
Other: body dysmorphic disorder.

Course: Admitted from the ED after the roommate reported suicidal talk and stockpiled medication. On the unit she was withdrawn for the first two days, then engaged in groups and individual sessions. No self-harm on the unit. Denied hallucinations during the stay. With her consent, her roommate brought in and turned over the saved tablets. A written safety plan was completed with her and her mother. Sertraline 50 mg daily continued unchanged. At discharge she denied suicidal intent, was future oriented, and had a therapy appointment booked for 6/6.

Discharge medications: sertraline 50 mg daily, dispensed two weeks at a time for now.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: therapist 6/6; outpatient psychiatry within 2 weeks; primary care within 1 week.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after discharge summary arrived. Pt home since yesterday, staying with her mother this week. Has her sertraline, has her safety plan, therapy tomorrow. Denies thoughts of harming herself today. Scheduled with PCP 6/10. Reviewed 988 and ED instructions.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. ED record and psychiatry discharge summary reviewed. Her mother sat in for part of the visit with Paige's okay.

She says the weeks before were "a fog." She had let therapy lapse in the spring and stopped answering messages. She is embarrassed about it but glad the roommate called. Saw her therapist on 6/6 and has psychiatry next week. Taking sertraline 50 daily; pharmacy is giving two weeks at a time.

Asked directly: no current thoughts of killing herself, no plan. No saved pills at home now; her mother checked. No firearms in the home.

Exam: tired appearing, eye contact fair, speech soft but coherent. Weight 60.8. Heart and lungs normal.

PHQ-9: 13.

A/P:
1. Suicidal ideation, recent admission. Safety plan reviewed line by line; it's in her phone and on the fridge. Keep therapy weekly, psychiatry next week.
2. Schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, and BDD: per psychiatry, sertraline unchanged.
3. Nurse call in a month. Message me any time.
RTC 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Pharmacy call
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacist called to confirm the sertraline is meant to be dispensed 14 days at a time. Confirmed per the psychiatry discharge plan; psychiatry is the prescriber and will decide when to lift it. Pharmacist will note it on the profile.

documents.title: Nurse check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Monthly check-in call. Pt reports she is back to weekly therapy and saw psychiatry on schedule. Mood "a bit better, up and down." Denies suicidal thoughts. Sleeping okay. Sertraline daily. No questions for PCP. Reminded her of her September follow-up.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PSYCHIATRY GROUP
Follow-up, 8/19/2025
Re: Paige Howland

About 11 weeks out from her inpatient stay for suicidal ideation. Attending therapy weekly again. Mood improved but fragile. No suicidal thoughts in the past month. No hallucinations. Appearance preoccupation unchanged.

Medication: sertraline 50 mg daily, taking consistently. Pharmacy back to 30-day fills from this visit.

Plan: continue sertraline 50 mg daily, weekly therapy, safety plan in place. Follow up in 4 to 5 months.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Cancelled visit
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel tomorrow's follow-up, teaching a section at that time this semester. Says she is doing okay and is seeing psychiatry and therapy. Will book her physical in the winter instead. PCP aware.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2025-26 flu and COVID given. Asked how she is doing: "better than spring." No thoughts of self-harm. Tolerated vaccines.
